title: The Office (US)
note: Written by Claude for Watch Together. Moments are approximate (fraction of the runtime, in scene order).

items.fact: Season 4 opened with an hour-long episode, often split into two parts on streaming services.
Michael convinces himself the office is cursed after hitting Meredith with his car in the parking lot.
At the hospital it turns out Meredith has rabies, which inspires Michael's charity race.
The full name of Michael's race is 'Michael Scott's Dunder Mifflin Scranton Meredith Palmer Memorial Celebrity Rabies Awareness Pro-Am Fun Run Race for the Cure'.
Angela's cat Sprinkles dies because Dwight froze it – a sore point that fuels their break-up later in the season.
This is the episode where Jim and Pam finally admit to the documentary crew that they are dating.
Ryan comes back to Scranton as Michael's boss, pitching the company's new website, Dunder Mifflin Infinity.
Michael tries to win back clients by delivering gift baskets in person – old-school sales versus Ryan's web strategy.
'The machine knows!' – Michael follows his GPS straight into a lake while Dwight shouts that it's a lake. It is one of the show's most quoted scenes.
Ryan's stubble-and-dark-clothes makeover marks his slide into the 'Wunderkind' arc that ends with his arrest later this season.
The office watches the website launch over a video feed, assuming they're invited to the New York party.
Dwight challenges the website to a sales race – man against machine.
Michael keeps the pizza delivery boy hostage over a coupon dispute – a scene fans still quote as 'the pizza hostage'.
The running joke: everyone knows to order from Alfredo's Pizza Cafe, never Pizza by Alfredo.
Jan's spending has buried Michael in debt, so he takes a night job as a telemarketer.
Jim and Pam stay at Dwight's beet farm, now a bed and breakfast (agritourism) listed on travel sites.
Jim tells Pam that whenever he feels down he goes to the stairwell – a sweet callback that fans love.
'I DECLARE BANKRUPTCY!' – Michael's shouted declaration is one of the show's best-known lines.
This episode was directed by film director Jason Reitman (Juno, Up in the Air).
Dwight plays the online world Second Life – and inside it he plays a game called 'Second Second Life'.
Michael's homemade ad replaces the professional one; the whole office ends up cheering for it.
Karen is now regional manager in Utica and tries to poach Stanley.
Pam, Oscar and Toby's Finer Things Club bans talk of work and TV – and refuses to let Jim join.
Michael, Dwight and Jim break into the Utica branch in disguise and steal a copier.
Michael wasn't invited to Ryan's executive wilderness retreat, so he stages his own survival trip.
Meanwhile Jim tries to merge all the office birthday parties into one – and learns how hard Michael's job is.
Dwight secretly watches over Michael in the woods to make sure he survives.
Jan is suing Dunder Mifflin for wrongful termination and expects Michael to support her.
Jan's lawyer reads Michael's private diary out loud during the deposition.
Back in the office, Kevin and Darryl get into a fierce ping-pong rivalry.
'Dinner Party' was the first new episode after the 2007–08 Writers Guild strike.
Michael's prized plasma TV is famously tiny – the camera keeps catching it.
Jan's candle company 'Serenity by Jan' makes the condo smell overwhelming.
'Snip snap, snip snap' – Michael reveals he's had three vasectomies (and reversals).
Jan plays 'That One Night', a song by her former assistant Hunter, to make Michael jealous.
Jan throws one of Michael's Dundie awards at his TV; the episode is regularly ranked among the best in the series.
Michael falls for the model in an office-chair catalog and tries to find her.
Meanwhile Dwight gives questionable legal advice to Andy about his car.
This episode was written by Mindy Kaling, who plays Kelly Kapoor.
Michael and Dwight visit Ryan in New York and see how far his party lifestyle has gone.
The Scranton crew gets locked inside the office building's gate overnight.
Toby puts his hand on Pam's knee – then announces he's moving to Costa Rica and runs out.
Stanley's 'Did I stutter?' at a meeting is one of the rare times the quiet salesman openly defies Michael.
Michael is torn between being liked and being respected – a central theme of his character.
Michael and Pam staff a job fair at Michael's old high school with almost no candidates.
Jim, Andy and Kevin play golf to win a client – Andy's preppy confidence goes badly.
Pam decides to apply to art school – the Pratt Institute in New York.
The Season 4 finale was an hour long, split into two parts on streaming.
Michael plans a lavish farewell party for Toby – mostly because he's thrilled Toby is leaving.
Holly Flax arrives: Amy Ryan joined the show the same season she earned an Oscar nomination for 'Gone Baby Gone'.
Michael convinces Holly that Kevin has a mental disability, leading to one of the season's most awkward running gags.
Jim was planning to propose to Pam that night, but Andy proposes to Angela first and Jim backs off.
Ryan is arrested for fraud over the Dunder Mifflin Infinity website.
Season 5 starts with a summer-long weight-loss competition between the branches.
Pam leaves for art school in New York, putting her and Jim into a long-distance relationship.
Michael and Holly's romance begins in earnest in this episode.
Jim proposes to Pam at a highway rest stop in the rain – the production built a full replica rest stop, reportedly about $250,000, the show's most expensive shot.
Holly runs a business-ethics seminar, and Meredith admits she slept with a supplier for discounts.
Jim times how long Dwight spends on personal stuff at work and confronts him with the total.
Jan's baby shower is held at the office even though she isn't sure Michael is involved at all.
Michael practises driving to the hospital with Dwight – it goes badly.
After a burglary, Michael throws a charity auction to replace what was stolen.
Corporate transfers Holly to the Nashua branch after learning about her relationship with Michael.
Michael and Dwight drive Holly to Nashua; the goodbye is one of the show's saddest moments.
Jim and Dwight get low customer-satisfaction scores, which threatens their bonuses.
It turns out Kelly and Ryan changed the scores – Kelly as payback for Jim missing her party.
Michael, Andy and Oscar go on a sales trip to Winnipeg, Canada.
Pam admits to Jim that she failed a course and will be stuck in New York another term.
Toby returns from Costa Rica, to Michael's horror.
Michael tries to frame Toby by planting what he thinks is marijuana – it's actually a caprese salad.
Jim buys his parents' house as a surprise for Pam.
Michael must choose how to spend a $4,300 budget surplus: a new copier or new chairs.
He finally learns that whatever he doesn't spend, he gets a percentage of as a bonus.
Dwight corners the market on a hit doll, Princess Unicorn, and resells it at a markup.
Meredith's hair catches fire at the party – the start of Michael's 'intervention'.
Phyllis reveals Angela and Dwight's affair to get back at Angela for taking over the party.
Andy learns about Angela and Dwight – and challenges Dwight to a duel.
The 'duel' becomes a slow-speed car fight in a parking lot with a tiny Prius.
Michael and Dwight go undercover to get client names from a small family-run paper company.
Michael regrets it when he meets the friendly family he's about to put out of business.
This hour-long episode aired right after Super Bowl XLIII in 2009.
Dwight's fake fire drill – including throwing Angela's cat into the ceiling – is one of the most celebrated cold opens in TV.
The CPR class turns into chaos; the dummy ends up wearing Dwight's face.
Jim and Pam watch a bootleg film starring Jack Black, Jessica Alba and Cloris Leachman – cameos shot for the episode.
Michael asks the office to roast him to relieve stress – and takes it far too personally.
Michael tours other branches to give motivational talks about Scranton's success.
Michael insists on stopping in Nashua to see Holly – and learns she has a new boyfriend.
Michael hides 'golden tickets' in paper boxes, Willy Wonka style – and it goes very wrong.
When it turns out to be a success, Dwight takes the credit.
Idris Elba guest-stars as the strict new VP Charles Miner.
Michael quits after 15 years at Dunder Mifflin, setting up the Michael Scott Paper Company arc.
Michael tries to recruit people for his new company during his two weeks' notice.
Pam quits to join him as a saleswoman – a big turn for her character.
The Michael Scott Paper Company starts in a tiny office space in the same building.
Michael and Dwight compete to steal each other's clients.
The MSPC's prices are so low that every sale loses money.
Dunder Mifflin buys the company back and Michael negotiates jobs for Pam and Ryan as salespeople.
Casual Friday turns ugly when Meredith takes it too far.
Michael turns the MSPC's old office into an espresso-and-disco bar.
Michael and Holly perform a sketch based on 'Slumdog Millionaire' – and accidentally announce branch closings.
Season 5 ends with a cut-off scene at a doctor's office: Pam is pregnant.
